novelty_flags.label: thm:oracle-preservation and related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The proposal says the anchor's feasible discussion invokes a regular parametric model, but arXiv:2506.18215v1 formulates its fixed-quantile theorem with observed true e(X) and supplies no such feasible theorem.

novelty_flags.label: thm:oracle-preservation
novelty_flags.one_line: Calling the result a strict extension of the oracle anchor is unsupported while it narrows to P_S and takes the decisive tail-relative-error condition E_{a,n}M_n^{gamma_a-1}=o_P(1) as a premise rather than deriving it for the displayed learner.

soundness_flags.label: ass:uniform-chart
soundness_flags.one_line: Uniform covariate chart is a paper-specific coordinate restriction, not a standard condition under the supplied name/citation; retag it novel and justify the restriction.

soundness_flags.label: ass:opposite-overlap
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited anchor does not impose a fixed bound away from the opposite endpoint, so this is a nonstandard subclass restriction that must be tagged novel and justified.

soundness_flags.label: def:hall-class, def:smooth-class, prop:smooth-inclusion, thm:joint-qte
soundness_flags.one_line: The core never defines “heavy arm”; its advertised center has pi_0(x)=1-x^{3/2}/2 bounded below by 1/2, so it has no positive-c Hall lower tail or gamma_0 despite later two-arm statements requiring an index and normalization for every arm.

soundness_flags.label: thm:gaussian-branch
soundness_flags.one_line: On the proposal's bounded-control center, h_hat_{0,n} is asymptotically 2 and b_hat_{0,n} tends to vartheta_0/2; the allowed grid permits vartheta_0>1, causing nonvanishing clipping and a different population weighted quantile, so the asserted root-n expansion around q_0 fails.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3, “IPW estimation for fixed quantiles,” pp. 4–5; equations defining X_n and qhat_n; Theorem 3.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The theorem's observed vectors explicitly include e(X_i), and its objective weights by max{e(X_i),b_n}; this is a true-propensity oracle theorem, not a theorem for a regular parametric fitted propensity. The section only assumes e(X_i) lies in (0,1), not a fixed opposite-endpoint separation.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section on optimal nonparametric regression rates, Assumption “Hölder smoothness and fixed domain”
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Dorn fixes X uniformly distributed on a hypercube explicitly “for convenience” inside a particular Hölder regression model; it is not presented as a standard condition named “Uniform covariate chart.”

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair the arm-regime definition: either require a Hall tail with declared gamma_a for both arms, or explicitly split Hall-tail and bounded-away arms and define their thresholds, clipping, and normalizations separately.
Restrict the clipping grid so bounded-away arms have b_hat_{a,n} below their support infimum (or set their clipping to zero), then restate and recheck the Gaussian and mixed-arm sanity reductions.

Replace the E_{a,n}M_n^{gamma_a-1}=o_P(1) premise with a derived tail-band theorem for the stated spline learner, or make that derivation a sharply named OEQ and remove “strict extension” language until it is proved.

Correct the Avella-Medina et al. comparison to a true-propensity oracle theorem and retag the uniform-chart and opposite-endpoint restrictions as novel subclass conditions with independent applicability justification.

recommended_next_step: Return to Stage -1 for a substantive rewrite before Stage 0: repair the Gaussian-arm clipping contradiction and arm-regime definitions, then re-submit the conditional learned-tail novelty claim with an accurate oracle comparator.
